answer_text: Yes, by its own account. Hex says an attacker used a flaw to run commands on six hex.pm web servers for about 13 minutes on Nov 23. It found no sign packages were changed, but cannot rule out that account data was read.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Were any Hex packages tampered with?
answer_text: Hex says no: every release published during the attack matches its audit log, no older release changed, and package files match the checksums in its database. That is Hex's own check; nobody outside has published one.
label: Reported

question_text: Do I need to change my Hex password?
answer_text: If you have a hex.pm account, yes: Hex asks you to change your password, set up 2FA again and update your Hex client when the new release is out. If you only download public packages and never made an account, there is nothing to reset.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Was my Hex account data taken?
what_would_settle_it: Hex saying whether its further investigation found that data was read, or evidence of the data being used or offered.

question_text: Who was behind the Hex.pm attack?
what_would_settle_it: Hex, law enforcement or a credible independent analysis naming the attacker.

question_text: Which organisations use Hex, and were they affected?
answer_text: Not publicly known. Hex names no customers, and no organisation has said it was affected. Hex says it will contact affected organisations with private packages directly.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: An organisation saying it uses Hex and whether it was affected, or Hex naming affected customers.

question_text: Has Hex finished replacing its registry signing key?
what_would_settle_it: Hex releasing the new Hex client with its new registry signing system, as it says it will in the coming days.
